_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a pal_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Pal Data vs Pal Instance). Adding a species is an edit to this file and to the `creatures` block of data/config/art.json, and to nothing else.
_comment_roster:
M11. The roster is named FROM the pack, per docs/decisions/D04 — GAME_DESIGN.md §26 lists ecological ROLES, not names, and says the final ones should be chosen around the best cohesive asset set. That set is the Quaternius Ultimate Animated Animal Pack plus two models from his Easy Enemy Pack: fourteen models, one artist, one faceted flat-material language, CC0 (docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md).

EIGHT of §26's sixteen slots are filled and eight are deliberately EMPTY. The pack contains no bird of any kind, no turtle and no otter, and no other free pack matches this one's style closely enough to borrow one — which under D04 costs more in cohesion than a role is worth. So there is no Air starter, no Water starter, no small bird, no owl, no hawk, no turtle, no otter and no waterfowl. An honest roster of eight beats a padded sixteen, and the empty roles are recorded here rather than filled with something that reads wrong.
_comment_types:
Every species carries a `type` from GAME_DESIGN.md §8's locked eight. NOTHING IN THE GAME READS IT — there is no chart, no multiplier and no same-type bonus, and §8 says the chart must exist before full Meadows balancing. Building it is a separate system and a design decision above M11's remit, so the field is data and inert on purpose.

The roster is 7 Ground and 1 Water, which is a fact about the pack rather than a balance choice: Meadows' dominant type is Ground (§9, §26) and the only non-terrestrial model in fourteen is a frog. Dual typing (§8, 'exists but is uncommon') is not expressible here either — `type` is one string — and that is left for whoever builds the chart.
_comment_size:
Heights are the GAMEPLAY size. pal_body._fit() measures the model and scales it to this, so the collider, the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus never move when the art is swapped, and so a species' size is data.

The cast spans 0.36m to 2.10m — 5.8x, against Palworld's ~6x and against the 1.8x MA-04 measured and failed the roster on. Two creatures are taller than the 1.80m trainer and the smallest is barely above his knee. The sizes are meant to say what the roles say: the tutorial creature is something you could pick up, the ambusher is bigger than you are, the mount is the tallest thing in the meadow, and the evolution is a head taller than what it evolved from.
_comment_footprint: `footprint_allowance` is how long a body may be for its width, as a multiple of its collider diameter. A quadruped is genuinely several times longer than it is wide; a frog is not. Set too low and pal_body._fit() scales the model DOWN to fit the allowance and the creature renders shorter than its own collider claims — silently, until MA-04. Every value here is computed from the model's own measured bounds (tools/preview_roster_ingame.gd -- probe) with ~15% of headroom, not guessed.
_comment_art: `model` is fitted at load; `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule a missing model renders as. Per-material colours live in data/config/art.json under `creatures.retint`, keyed by species and then by the material name inside the .gltf — the same mechanism vegetation.json uses on foliage, and for the same reason: the pack ships flat named material zones and no textures, so a name is a stable handle and a hue is one line.
_comment_animations:
Clip names are per-pack and live here so a new creature is a data edit. This pack ships three different naming conventions in one family — the big quadrupeds call their attack `Attack_Headbutt`, the canids call it `Attack`, and the two Easy Enemy models namespace everything as `RatArmature|Rat_Idle`. Nothing in code knows any of that.

Two species are missing clips and it is recorded rather than hidden: the frog has no walk (it hops, which is arguably correct for a frog) so its walk and run are both its jump; and neither the frog nor the rat has a hit reaction, so those two simply do not flinch. pal_animator.play_once() refuses to fall back onto the idle for a missing one-shot — holding locomotion off for the whole length of an idle clip is a creature frozen for three seconds every time it is hit, which is far worse than a missing flinch.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild pal will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md §14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL pal, and the same list allows 'Aggressive pal initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.
_comment_legendary: §28's unique Ground legendary — the ultimate riding mount — IS NOT HERE, and that is a decision. No free finished asset carries it; the sourcing pass established that and separately flagged that §28 wants Ground while every awe-inspiring free candidate is a flyer. The nearest thing in this pack is the Stag, and a scaled-up Stag standing next to `wild_grazer` — which IS the Stag — would be the padding this roster is meant not to do. docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md records the real answer: Quaternius ships the CC0 .blend sources, so the legendary does not have to be bought, it has to be MODELLED from a rigged antlered base. Until it is, M14's slot is empty and says so.
_comment_evolution: §11: evolution is limited, starters do not evolve, some rare pals do, and it 'must visually make sense with available assets'. One line exists — `wild_pup` into `evolved_wolf` — and `evolves_into` is inert data: no code reads it, because the requirement (level + high bond + item) is a system nobody has built. What it does today is let tests/test_roster.gd assert the thing that was WRONG when the pack landed: at the pack's own scale the ShibaInu is 0.94m and the Wolf is 0.80m, so the evolution SHRANK. Sizes here are authored, not inherited, and the evolved form is a head taller and more than twice as long.

starter_ground._comment:
THE GROUND STARTER, and the only starter that exists. §26 wants three — Ground durable/forgiving, Water balanced/efficient, Air aggressive/fast-energy — and the pack has no flyer and only one aquatic model, which the Water common wild role has a better claim on. So Water and Air starters are absent. Ground is the one §26 names first and the one the Meadows is built around.

Durable and forgiving reads out of the numbers: the highest defence in the roster, high HP, and the second-lowest attack of anything that fights. It survives your mistakes and it does not win fast.
starter_ground._comment_model: The Alpaca, at 1.25m — chest-high on the trainer, so it reads as a companion rather than as livestock. Chosen over the two dogs because it is the only upright, compact, non-quadruped-slab silhouette in the pack (0.80 long-for-tall against the Wolf's 2.07), which keeps the creature you see in every single frame from being one more low brown four-legged thing. Retinted to the most saturated warm amber in the roster for MA-02's stated reason: your own pal must never be the least readable object in your own fight.

wild_rabbit._comment: §26's rabbit role: Ground, common, the tutorial creature. Peaceful, generous to catch, and the weakest thing in the biome by a clear margin — it is the one the owner will throw at twenty times while deciding whether throwing is fun, and a rare or a stubborn target would make that a test of patience instead.
wild_rabbit._comment_model: The Easy Enemy Pack's Rat, at 0.36m — knee-high on the trainer, and the smallest thing in the roster. That is the point: MA-04's scale criterion failed a cast that spanned 1.8x with 'nothing small enough to be cute-underfoot', and this is the small end of the 5.8x the roster now spans. Retinted to the bright gold the previous roster used for this same role, at value 0.95, because it is the creature that most has to be findable in grass.

placeholder._comment_animations: No hit reaction in the pack. It does not flinch; see the roster-level animation note.

wild_croaker._comment: §26's frog/newt role: the common Water species, and the ONLY Water species in the Meadows. Balanced — no stat is a standout — because it is the creature that teaches you that not everything in the meadow is Ground, and a common should not also be a puzzle.
wild_croaker._comment_model: The Easy Enemy Pack's Frog at 0.42m, wider than it is deep and barely taller than the grass. Green on green is the readability defect the sourcing pass named on this exact model — the pack ships its body as #80a960, which is the meadow's own hue — so it is retinted to a saturated water blue with a gold belly. A frog that is water-coloured rather than leaf-coloured also says which type it is before any UI does.

placeholder._comment_animations: No walk and no hit reaction. Walk and run are both the hop, deliberately: a frog that slides across the ground on its idle is worse than a frog that hops everywhere.

wild_stalker._comment: §26's badger role: Ground, aggressive, uncommon. The glass cannon of the roster — the highest attack of anything below the evolved form and the lowest defence of anything that starts fights. It hurts and it folds, which is a different fight from the Thornback's and is the reason both exist.
wild_stalker._comment_model: The Fox at 0.68m: low, long (2.19 long-for-tall) and fast-reading, which is the silhouette an ambusher wants. Retinted crimson — the pack's own #b67343 fox-orange collides with the starter's amber, and two hue-adjacent creatures in one frame is the cohesion complaint MA-02 made about the last roster.

wild_pup._comment: §26's 'young canine → wolf', the rare evolution line, and §11's own worked example. Peaceful, rare, and deliberately unremarkable on paper: it is the weakest thing in the roster after the tutorial creature, because everything it is worth is what it becomes. A player who catches one and reads its card should be underwhelmed and then, much later, not.
wild_pup._comment_model: The ShibaInu at 0.85m. Coloured as a pale, low-saturation version of the Gloamfang's indigo with the same amber eye, so the two read as one creature at two ages rather than as a dog and a wolf that happen to be linked in a table.

evolved_wolf._comment:
The Meadows' one evolved form. The strongest catchable creature in the biome and the only one that beats the Thornback on every stat — an evolution that is merely sideways is not worth the level, the bond and the item §11 asks for.

Rare in the wild on purpose: the intended way to own one is to raise a Duskpup, and finding a grown one should feel like meeting something that got there first.
evolved_wolf._comment_model:
The Wolf, at 1.35m and 2.8m long — against the Duskpup's 0.85m and 1.1m. THIS IS THE FIX FOR THE SCALE INVERSION: at the pack's uniform 0.32 the ShibaInu measures 0.94m and the Wolf 0.80m, so the evolution physically shrank. Sizes are authored per species, so the evolved form is now a head taller than the trainer's waist, more than twice as long as the pup, and reads as the bigger, more dangerous thing before any number is shown.

The pack ships it as #777972 — pale grey at almost exactly the meadow's own value, which is the second readability defect the sourcing pass found and is MA-02's 'your own pal is the least readable object in your own fight' returning as an opponent. Retinted to a deep saturated indigo with a pale cold ruff and amber eyes: hue-opposed to a green world, high internal value contrast, and legibly the adult of the Duskpup's palette.

wild_bristler._comment: §26's boar role: Ground, bulky, aggressive. The one that comes at you — tougher and rarer than the Hopper, because being ambushed should be a moment rather than an interruption, and because the first thing anyone does when something charges them is find out whether they can beat it. It is beatable: the starter out-defends it and out-lasts it, and loses only to being greedy.
wild_bristler._comment_model: The Bull at 1.95m and 3.4m long, which makes it the first creature in this project that is BIGGER THAN THE TRAINER — MA-04's scale finding, in one species. Dark warm umber so it holds a heavy silhouette against grass, with bone horns and amber eyes as the two bright marks that say which end is dangerous.

wild_grazer._comment:
§26's 'deer/horse-like — rideable' role, and M12's mount. Enormous HP, the highest defence in the roster and the lowest attack of anything catchable: it is not a fighter and the numbers say so before the player finds out. Rare and peaceful.

Only ONE rideable, where §26 implies a family. The pack holds a Deer, a Donkey, two Horses and a Cow that would all fill the same slot, and shipping four large brown quadrupeds with different names is exactly the padding this roster refuses. The Stag has the one silhouette among them nobody would mistake for another.
wild_grazer._comment_model: The Stag at 2.10m to the antler tips — the tallest creature in the Meadows and a head above the trainer. Retinted to warm ivory with dark antlers, muzzle and hooves: near-white against olive is the largest value separation available, it does not repeat any other creature's hue, and a pale hart is a thing you would ride. The body is ONE material — it has no separately-coloured legs and never had — so the antlers carry the whole silhouette, which is the weakest thing about this species in the rendered sheet.
